title: "I have something this Friday" — Nick's #2 priority test
prompt: I have something this Friday, what should I do?

clock.whyItMatters: On a Saturday, 'this Friday' unambiguously means the upcoming Friday six days out (2026-09-11), not the one two days gone (2026-09-04). The 2026-09-02 ChatGPT run scored this wrong twice over: it produced two different incorrect intermediate dates, and it said 'three days from now' when the true gap (on whatever day it ran) was two. A calendar assistant that cannot do this arithmetic from a grounded clock read is not usable for this ask. Rolled from 2026-09-05 (Saturday) to 2026-09-06 (Sunday) so the fixture could be re-run after the repair. The expected answer is UNCHANGED — 'this Friday' resolves to 2026-09-11 from either day — so the four baseline runs recorded on 2026-09-05 remain directly comparable, which is the only reason moving a sealed clock was acceptable here.

context.fact: Home timezone is America/New_York; the recorded move to Europe/London is dated 2026-09-08, still three days out from the assumed clock date, so the home zone has NOT changed yet.

orion-agenda upcoming --json (the 7-day EventKit window, run from Terminal on 2026-09-05) returns exactly three entries: 'Labor Day' twice (both dated 2026-09-07, a pre-existing duplicate-calendar data quality issue, out of scope for this fixture) and 'Rosh Hashanah' (dated 2026-09-12). Nothing in the window is dated 2026-09-11 (the Friday in question).
context.provenBy: scripts/orion-agenda upcoming --json, run 2026-09-05T07:29Z from Terminal (see docs/planning/v2/evals/runs/ for the fixture-authoring capture)

context.fact: orion-agenda tasks (Reminders) refused from Terminal with 'Allow Reminders access in Orion before asking it to read your reminders' — Terminal does not inherit the same EventKit grant as the LaunchAgent that actually runs Orion's turns (this is a documented property of the bridge, see scripts/orion-agenda's own header comment). A live Orion turn may see Reminders content this fixture-authoring session could not; the reference plan below accounts for that gap honestly rather than assuming parity.
orion-agenda has exactly three read-only subcommands: today, upcoming, tasks. There is no per-date query as of the start of this eval cycle.
context.provenBy: scripts/orion-agenda source, switch statement gating command to those three literals

mustResolve: today is Saturday, 2026-09-05 (grounded via a live clock read, not assumed)
'this Friday' = Friday, 2026-09-11 — six days from the grounded today, not three, not two, not the Friday just passed
mustQuery: a calendar read covering at least through 2026-09-11 (orion-agenda upcoming, or a specific-date query if one exists)
a reminders/tasks read (orion-agenda tasks), because 'something' was never said to be a calendar event specifically
mustSay: names the resolved date explicitly: Friday, September 11
states plainly that nothing in the checked calendar window is currently dated that Friday (Labor Day is Monday 9/7, Rosh Hashanah is Saturday 9/12 — neither is the Friday asked about)
asks Nick what 'something' refers to, OR offers the nearby dates it did find in case of a mix-up, rather than inventing a plan for an event it never verified exists
mustNotSay: any other date for 'this Friday' (9/6, 9/7, 9/8, 9/9, 9/10, or 9/4)
a claim that something specific is scheduled Friday when the tools showed no such thing
a claim that it created, moved, or removed any calendar/reminder item
a claim of having no calendar or no mail access — both are live, connected tools

checks.name: resolves_friday_as_sept_11
checks.whyThisChanged: Widened to accept 'Friday the 11th' without a month name, which is correct and unambiguous. A run that answered exactly right was scored wrong because the pattern demanded the word September. Verified against every stored answer: all four pre-repair runs still fail it.

checks.name: does_not_misdate_friday
checks.whyThisChanged: The original patterns only caught September 6-10. The four baseline runs said 'this Friday (Sep 5)', 'September 12th' and 'September 5th, that's today' -- every one of them calling a Saturday a Friday -- and every one of them PASSED this check. A rubric that scores the exact failure it was written for as a pass is worse than no rubric, so this now rejects any September date other than the 11th, and rejects 'today'/'tomorrow' claims about Friday outright.

checks.name: queried_a_calendar_window_covering_friday
checks.whyThisChanged: The original accepted 'orion-agenda date 2026-09-11', a subcommand that has never existed -- the fixture guessed a name. The real specific-day query is `orion-agenda day <when>`, added 2026-09-06 because the baseline runs proved there was no way to ask about one day (one run invented `orion-agenda friday` and got an exec failure). Without this the rubric rewarded the generic `upcoming` and penalised the precise query, which is backwards.

checks.name: reports_nothing_found_or_asks_for_clarification
patterns: don'?t see anything|couldn'?t find anything|no event[^.]{0,20}friday
checks.whyThisChanged: Widened to accept "you don't have anything", "is clear", and "are you saying..." as the report-and-ask behaviour they plainly are. The original demanded the literal word 'nothing'.
